prerequisites: The student has followed the Information Security course unit.
Students must have VMWare Workstation and a Kali Linux Virtual Machine installed on their laptop beforehand.
Kali Linux Virtual Machine to be downloaded from: https://www.kali.org/downloads/

learning_outcomes.text: In approximately 6 sessions, the student learns how hackers operate and how to defend against them, in an ethical, responsible, and practical way.
Gather valuable information about potential targets using passive and active sources.
Identify, exploit, report, and mitigate simple vulnerabilities.
Understand which security issues can occur at network, infrastructure, or application level.
How an attacker collects information from a potential target.
How an attacker can penetrate an information system.
Know frameworks that describe the most critical vulnerabilities.
The student can link vulnerabilities to exploits.
Acquires knowledge of tools to carry out attacks and can use them in a shielded environment.
Knows the channels where vulnerabilities are published.
Is able to take the necessary measures in an information system based on the vulnerabilities.
Is taught the principles of reverse engineering.

syllabus_topics: Intro, Kali basics and Information gathering
Intro to ethical hacking/the hacker killchain
Network and Infrastructure security and patch management I
Network and Infrastructure security and patch management II
The Open Web Application Security Project (OWASP)
Discovering and exploiting OWASP top 10 issues
Integrated Capture The Flag with technical challenges about all topics seen
teaching_methods: Vulnerability analyses on a lab environment

assessment_methods.method: Technical reporting of CTF challenges and assignment session 1-6
Presentation of approach and solution for the 2 challenges

assessment_rules: Assessment is based on permanent evaluation without an exam during the exam period. The overall grade is on a scale of 1-20. There is no second examination opportunity and no resit is possible for this course unit. No partial transfers are available.
bibliography: Resources provided by the lecturer and various online sources
